answer: An agent market requires every seller to lock $100 in escrow for as long as it trades, plus 30 days after exit. A thousand fake sellers therefore immobilize $100,000, imposing a capital cost even if none cheats. A polished profile may whisper credibility, but that signal is hollow without the bond; even an account preserved as a relic of the market’s early days must pay. Creating names is cheap; funding each active name is costly.
